main_result: For every n≥2 and every simple graph H with h≥1 edges and at most n vertices, the containment threshold pc(n,H) (the p at which G(n,p) contains an ordinary copy of H with probability 1/2) satisfies pc(n,H) ≤ min{1, 2048·e^50·pE(n,H)·(1+log2 h)}, where pE is the graph expectation threshold (least p at which every subgraph F⊆H has E[copies of F] ≥ 1/2). Hence pc(n,H) ≤ 6144·e^50·pE(n,H)·log2 n. This is a single-logarithm version of the second Kahn–Kalai conjecture for graphs. I checked the arithmetic of the constants (2048 = 16·128, 6144 = 3·2048, 1+log2 h ≤ 3 log2 n for n≥2) and they are consistent.
proof_strategy: Step 1 (graph hierarchy): for each current edge set I⊆H, pick a subgraph S⊆I maximizing σ^{-|S|}·P(fixed copy of S lies in a uniform copy of I), with σ=128·pE. The expectation constraints plus a binomial bound force |S|<|I|/17, giving a nested chain ∅=H_0⊂…⊂H_k=H with label sizes growing by a factor 16 and conditional spread σ. Step 2 (local resampling): with W~μ_ρ and a planted source label, the posterior-resampled target has small failure probability and a change-of-measure bound (distortion) of e^{11m} on functions of coordinates outside the target label. Step 3 (tree reduction): one shared W is used at all nodes; a recursive potential D bounds the probability that the root cannot be pruned to a good subtree (≤1/4), using disjointness so that D_b depends only on W outside the incoming label. Surviving nodes are reweighted, halving every capacity and multiplying spread by at most 4. Step 4 (iteration): about log2(ℓ_k) successful reductions are needed, each succeeding with probability ≥3/4; Markov's inequality and a union of 4s predrawn sets give the 2/3 probability. Monotonicity in r then yields the theorem. I verified each of these steps by hand; the parts I could only partly reconstruct are the detailed bookkeeping in the local lemma and the composition of recovery through iterations.
hardest_part: The most delicate point is the change-of-measure chain in Lemma 'Local resampling' (eq. distortion) combined with the potential recursion in the reduction lemma: one needs that the target posterior is bounded by e^{10m}·ν_b·ρ^{-|A_b|}, that the event A_b∖A_c⊆W is independent of f(W) for f depending only on W outside A_b, and that D_b depends only on W outside A_b because all labels below b are disjoint from A_b along paths. I checked each of these and they hold, but the manuscript compresses the exponent bookkeeping (the ρ^{-|A_b|} versus ρ^{|A_b∖A_c|} cancellation) and the indexing of levels in the potential, so I had to reconstruct these details myself.

main_result: For every n>=2 and every finite simple graph H with h>=1 edges and at most n vertices, pc(n,H) <= min{1, 2048 e^50 pE(n,H)(1+log2 h)}, where pc is the containment threshold (G(n,p) contains an ordinary copy of H with probability at least 1/2) and pE is the graph expectation threshold (every subgraph F of H has expected copy count at least 1/2). Since h <= n^2, this gives pc <= 6144 e^50 pE log2 n. This is the second Kahn-Kalai conjecture with an explicit universal constant.
proof_strategy: The argument reduces containment to a probabilistic statement about a random subset W of edges: a fixed tree of edge-set extensions, each level of which is sigma-spread with sigma = 128 pE, has a path union contained in W with probability at least 2/3 when W has density about 2048 e^50 pE(1+log2 h). The graph-specific tree (Lemma hierarchy) is built by repeatedly choosing a subgraph S of the current I that maximizes sigma^{-|S|} P(S_0 contained in a uniform copy of I); the first-moment constraint on pE forces |S| < |I|/17, so label sizes grow geometrically and spread follows from maximality. Tree covering (Theorem tree) iterates a one-level reduction (Lemma reduction) that resamples with a single shared product set W, using a Bayesian posterior transition whose local failure and change-of-measure are controlled by Lemma local resampling; a recursive potential D_v with a pruning rule shows the root survives with probability at least 3/4 per attempt. After about log2 l_k successful attempts all label capacities vanish, so the unions of the used draws contain a path union, and a Markov bound on the number of attempts gives probability at least 2/3. I checked the main inequalities (the failure bound e^{-9m}, the distortion bound e^{11m}, the potential recurrence and its unrolling, the geometric sum bounded below 1/4, the product bound below 4, and the constant 2048*3=6144) and found them consistent; the parts I could justify only by reconstructing unstated steps are noted below.
hardest_part: The step in Lemma reduction that asserts the spread of the reduced child law at fixed W, which rests on the claim that the source keeps its law nu_v at fixed W, together with the claim that D_b depends only on W outside A_b. I verified both after reconstruction, but they depend on independence of W and the source and on an induction over the subtree that the text only sketches. The iteration bookkeeping (cutting branches, composition of recovery, waiting-time domination) is the next least-verified part.

main_result: For every n≥2 and every simple graph H with h≥1 edges and at most n vertices, pc(n,H) ≤ min{1, 2048·e^{50}·pE(n,H)·(1+log2 h)}, where pc is the p at which G(n,p) contains H with probability at least 1/2 and pE is the least p at which every subgraph F of H has expected copy count at least 1/2. Since h ≤ n², this gives pc(n,H) ≤ 6144·e^{50}·pE(n,H)·log2 n. The proof is a single-logarithm bound (the second Kahn–Kalai conjecture, in this normalisation).
proof_strategy: A tree of successive edge extensions (copies of H_{i-1} extended to copies of H_i, with H_i chosen by maximising σ^{-|S|}·P(S₀⊆copy of I)) is built so that every level is σ-spread with σ=128·pE and capacities grow by a factor 16; I checked the maximality-based spread bound and the size bounds ℓ_{i+1}>16ℓ_i. Section 3 (tree covering) then reduces the tree level by level using one shared product sample W~μ_ρ: a local resampling step (Lemma local, with a failure bound e^{-9m} and a change-of-measure bound e^{11m}) is applied at every node, a recursive potential D_v with E D_v bounded by a geometric-type sum is used to show that with probability ≥3/4 the pruned tree succeeds, and the spread after conditioning is controlled by the source law. Iterating about s=⌊log2 ℓ_k⌋+1 times, with Markov's inequality on the number of attempts and a predrawn union of 4s product sets, gives the 2/3 probability bound at density r. I verified the constants (16·128=2048, 4sρ≤16e^{50}σs, the product bound below log 4) and the posterior/Bayes identity for the transition by direct computation. The Bayes identity for the target label is the part whose justification is least explicit in the text.
hardest_part: The transition in Section 2 (planted set W, source c, target b drawn from a posterior): the text computes the posterior of the source index given Y, but the target b is a separate random variable whose joint law with (c,W) is never specified. The bounds in Lemma local and in the reduction depend on P(target=b | W) = Σ_c ν_c ν_b ρ^{-|A_b|} 1{A_b⊆W∪A_c}/Z(W∪A_c), which I reconstructed myself rather than read off. I also could not confirm from the text alone that the reweighted child law after pruning is spread conditional on W in the way the next iteration requires, although I think the argument via T⊆A_c works.
